sources.summaryEn: Within-participant trial in 25 untrained men (each leg allocated to one of four protocols) doing 8 weeks of unilateral knee extension, volume-equated, at 80% 1RM to failure (~12.4 reps) or not (~6.7 reps), and 30% 1RM to failure (~34.4 reps) or not (~19.6 reps). Quadriceps CSA rose 8.1% (heavy, failure), 7.7% (heavy, non-failure) and 7.8% (light, failure), but only 2.8% (light, non-failure; not significant). 1RM gains were larger with heavy loads (about 33%) than light loads (about 16-18%). High effort mattered with light loads, where the non-failure sets stopped very far from failure, but added nothing with heavy loads.
sources.summaryPt: Ensaio intraindivíduo com 25 homens não treinados (cada perna alocada a um de quatro protocolos) fazendo 8 semanas de cadeira extensora unilateral, com volume equalizado, a 80% de 1RM até a falha (~12,4 repetições) ou não (~6,7 repetições), e a 30% de 1RM até a falha (~34,4 repetições) ou não (~19,6 repetições). A área de secção do quadríceps subiu 8,1% (carga alta, falha), 7,7% (carga alta, sem falha) e 7,8% (carga leve, falha), mas apenas 2,8% (carga leve, sem falha; não significativo). Os ganhos de 1RM foram maiores com carga alta (cerca de 33%) do que com carga leve (cerca de 16-18%). Esforço alto importou com cargas leves, em que as séries sem falha pararam muito longe da falha, mas não acrescentou nada com cargas altas.

sources.title: Large increases in resistance training volume do not impair muscle hypertrophy or anabolic-catabolic molecular signaling in trained individuals
sources.authors: Camargo JBB, Bittencourt D, Michel JM, Silva DG, Bergamasco JGA, Berry AC, et al., Roberts MD, Libardi CA
sources.summaryEn: Randomized, single-blind within-subject unilateral trial in 25 resistance-trained men and women (18-35 y) over 8 weeks (twice weekly). One leg increased weekly volume by 120% over habitual and the other by 20%. Vastus lateralis CSA increased in both legs with no protocol-by-time interaction. Fiber CSA, satellite-cell number and myonuclear content showed no significant changes, and most anabolic/catabolic signaling markers did not differ between protocols. A large abrupt increase neither enhanced nor impaired hypertrophy.
sources.summaryPt: Ensaio unilateral intraindivíduo, randomizado e simples-cego, com 25 homens e mulheres treinados (18-35 anos) durante 8 semanas (duas vezes por semana). Uma perna aumentou o volume semanal em 120% sobre o habitual e a outra em 20%. A área de secção transversa do vasto lateral aumentou nas duas pernas, sem interação protocolo-tempo. A área das fibras, o número de células satélites e o conteúdo mionuclear não mudaram significativamente, e a maioria dos marcadores de sinalização anabólica/catabólica não diferiu entre protocolos. Um aumento grande e abrupto não melhorou nem prejudicou a hipertrofia.

sources.title: Dumbbell versus cable lateral raises for lateral deltoid hypertrophy: an experimental study
sources.authors: Larsen S, Wolf M, Schoenfeld BJ, Sandberg NØ, Fredriksen AB, Kristiansen BS, van den Tillaar R, Swinton PA, Falch HN
sources.summaryEn: Twenty-four resistance-trained men and women (about 7 years of training) trained one arm with cable and the other with dumbbell lateral raises, arms randomised, for 8 weeks: 2 sessions per week, 5 sets to momentary failure, with shoulder ROM matched. The cable was set so peak torque fell near the bottom (adducted, lengthened) position, while the dumbbell loads the top most. Lateral deltoid thickness rose 3.3-4.6%, with moderate (univariate BF 0.22-0.27) to extreme (multivariate BF < 0.01) support for no difference. Shifting the resistance profile toward the lengthened position did not add growth here.
sources.summaryPt: Vinte e quatro homens e mulheres treinados em força (cerca de 7 anos de treino) treinaram um braço com elevação lateral no cabo e o outro com halter, com braços sorteados, por 8 semanas: 2 sessões por semana, 5 séries até a falha momentânea, com ROM do ombro pareada. O cabo foi ajustado para que o pico de torque ocorresse perto da posição inferior (aduzida, alongada), enquanto o halter carrega mais o topo. A espessura do deltoide lateral aumentou 3,3-4,6%, com suporte moderado (BF univariado 0,22-0,27) a extremo (BF multivariado < 0,01) à ausência de diferença. Deslocar o perfil de resistência para a posição alongada não acrescentou crescimento neste estudo.

sources.title: Muscle hypertrophy response across four muscles involved in the bench press exercise: Randomized 10 weeks training intervention
sources.authors: Lanza MB, Prado GC, Lacerda LT, Dinardi RR, Carvalho Junior LH, Diniz RC, Lima FV, Chagas MH, Martins-Costa HC
sources.journal: Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies
sources.summaryEn: Randomized trial in 24 healthy men (13 training, 11 controls) who performed only the bench press for 10 weeks: 3x/week, 3-4 sets of 12 reps at 50-55% 1RM, 36 s under tension per set, 3-min rest. Cross-sectional area was measured by MRI. Training increased the area of the pectoralis major, pectoralis minor, anterior deltoid and triceps brachii vs control; the medial deltoid was not among these. All of these muscles grew more than the medial deltoid, and the pectoralis major grew more than the pectoralis minor and triceps. Horizontal pressing therefore trains the front deltoid and triceps but gives the lateral deltoid the least stimulus; limitations are the small sample, unreported training status and a single low-load protocol.
sources.summaryPt: Ensaio randomizado com 24 homens saudáveis (13 treinando e 11 controles) que fizeram apenas supino por 10 semanas: 3x/semana, 3-4 séries de 12 repetições a 50-55% de 1RM, 36 s sob tensão por série e 3 min de descanso. A área de secção transversa foi medida por ressonância magnética. O treino aumentou a área do peitoral maior, do peitoral menor, do deltoide anterior e do tríceps braquial em relação ao controle; o deltoide medial não estava entre eles. Todos esses músculos cresceram mais que o deltoide medial, e o peitoral maior cresceu mais que o peitoral menor e o tríceps. Portanto, o supino horizontal treina o deltoide anterior e o tríceps, mas dá o menor estímulo ao deltoide lateral; as limitações são a amostra pequena, o nível de treinamento não informado e um único protocolo de carga baixa.

sources.title: Effects of Different Weekly Set Progressions on Muscular Adaptations in Trained Males: Is There a Dose–Response Effect?
sources.authors: Enes A, De Souza EO, Souza-Junior TP
sources.summaryEn: RCT in 31 resistance-trained men (about 5 years' experience) over 12 weeks of lower-body training twice weekly: constant volume vs adding 4 or 6 weekly sets every 2 weeks. Squat 1RM gains ranked +6 sets > +4 sets > constant (all pairwise differences significant). Vastus lateralis CSA and thigh thickness showed no significant group differences (p=0.067 and 0.076), although the confidence intervals suggested a possible small benefit that plateaued at the higher volumes. Small sample; the authors urge caution.
sources.summaryPt: ECR com 31 homens treinados (cerca de 5 anos de experiência) em 12 semanas de treino de membros inferiores duas vezes por semana: volume constante vs acréscimo de 4 ou 6 séries semanais a cada 2 semanas. Os ganhos de 1RM no agachamento seguiram a ordem +6 séries > +4 séries > constante (todas as diferenças entre pares significativas). A área de secção transversa do vasto lateral e a espessura da coxa não diferiram significativamente entre grupos (p=0,067 e 0,076), embora os intervalos de confiança sugiram um possível pequeno benefício que estabilizou nos volumes mais altos. Amostra pequena; os autores pedem cautela.

sources.title: High Resistance-Training Volume Enhances Muscle Thickness in Resistance-Trained Men
sources.authors: Brigatto FA, Lima LEM, Germano MD, Aoki MS, Braz TV, Lopes CR
sources.summaryEn: RCT in 27 resistance-trained men (pair-matched, then randomized) assigned to 16, 24 or 32 weekly sets per muscle group for 8 weeks, with all other variables held constant. All groups improved bench and squat 1RM and biceps, triceps and vastus lateralis thickness. 32 sets produced larger lower-body 1RM, vastus lateralis thickness and triceps thickness gains than 16 sets. Limitations: small groups (n=9 each) and short duration.
sources.summaryPt: ECR com 27 homens treinados (pareados e depois randomizados) alocados a 16, 24 ou 32 séries semanais por grupo muscular durante 8 semanas, com todas as outras variáveis mantidas constantes. Todos os grupos melhoraram o 1RM de supino e agachamento e a espessura de bíceps, tríceps e vasto lateral. 32 séries geraram ganhos maiores de 1RM de membros inferiores, de espessura do vasto lateral e de espessura do tríceps do que 16 séries. Limitações: grupos pequenos (n=9 cada) e duração curta.

sources.title: Progressive Resistance Training Volume: Effects on Muscle Thickness, Mass, and Strength Adaptations in Resistance-Trained Individuals
sources.authors: Aube D, Wadhi T, Rauch J, Anand A, Barakat C, Pearson J, Bradshaw J, Zazzo S, Ugrinowitsch C, De Souza EO
sources.summaryEn: RCT in 35 resistance-trained individuals (squat about 2.09× body mass) performing 12, 18 or 24 weekly lower-body sets, 2 sessions per week for 8 weeks. Muscle thickness and thigh fat-free mass rose similarly across groups (ΣMT +7.7%, +6.7% and +6.1% for 12, 18 and 24 sets). Squat 1RM tended (p=0.052) to favor 18 sets (+16.2%) over 24 sets (+5.4%), suggesting a middle dose for strength and no hypertrophy advantage above 12 sets.
sources.summaryPt: ECR com 35 indivíduos treinados (agachamento de cerca de 2,09× a massa corporal) realizando 12, 18 ou 24 séries semanais de membros inferiores, 2 sessões por semana durante 8 semanas. A espessura muscular e a massa magra da coxa aumentaram de forma semelhante entre os grupos (soma da espessura +7,7%, +6,7% e +6,1% para 12, 18 e 24 séries). O 1RM de agachamento tendeu (p=0,052) a favorecer 18 séries (+16,2%) em relação a 24 séries (+5,4%), sugerindo uma dose intermediária para força e nenhuma vantagem de hipertrofia acima de 12 séries.

sources.title: Exercise Dosing to Retain Resistance Training Adaptations in Young and Older Adults
sources.authors: Bickel CS, Cross JM, Bamman MM
sources.summaryEn: Two-phase trial in 70 adults (young 20-35 y and old 60-75 y): 16 weeks of resistance training 3 days per week, then 32 weeks of randomly assigned detraining or maintenance at one-third or one-ninth of the phase-1 dose. Both maintenance doses preserved muscle hypertrophy in the young (the one-third dose even added myofiber hypertrophy) but not in the old. Strength was largely retained even with detraining, with only a slight reduction at the final time point.
sources.summaryPt: Ensaio em duas fases com 70 adultos (jovens de 20-35 anos e idosos de 60-75 anos): 16 semanas de treino de força 3 dias por semana, seguidas de 32 semanas, com alocação aleatória, de destreino ou de manutenção com um terço ou um nono da dose da fase 1. As duas doses de manutenção preservaram a hipertrofia muscular nos jovens (a dose de um terço até acrescentou hipertrofia das fibras), mas não nos idosos. A força foi amplamente mantida mesmo com destreino, com apenas uma pequena queda no último momento avaliado.

sources.title: Resistance Training Recommendations to Maximize Muscle Hypertrophy in an Athletic Population: Position Stand of the IUSCA
sources.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Fisher JP, Grgic J, Haun CT, Helms ER, Phillips SM, Steele J, Vigotsky AD
sources.journal: International Journal of Strength and Conditioning
sources.summaryEn: Consensus of eight researchers on maximizing hypertrophy in athletes. Load: comparable hypertrophy across a wide spectrum of loads, prioritize moderate loads, and a combination of loading ranges may help (preliminary). Volume: about 10 sets per muscle per week is a general minimum, higher volumes may help underdeveloped muscles (specialization cycles), and weekly sets should rise by no more than 20% per ~4-week cycle. Frequency: no benefit when volume is equated, but cap per-session volume at about 10 sets per muscle and add frequency for more volume. Rest: at least 2 min on multi-joint and 60–90 s on single-joint or machine exercises. Exercise selection: mix multi- and single-joint exercises across planes and, where applicable, favor long muscle lengths. Novices need not train near failure, while highly trained lifters may take some sets to failure, conservatively and mainly on single-joint or machine exercises. Advanced techniques show no empirical hypertrophy advantage but no apparent harm, and cardio does not seem to interfere at moderate volumes (separate sessions or lift first). Narrative consensus without formal evidence grading.
sources.summaryPt: Consenso de oito pesquisadores sobre como maximizar a hipertrofia em atletas. Carga: hipertrofia comparável em uma ampla faixa de cargas, priorizar cargas moderadas, e combinar faixas de carga pode ajudar (evidência preliminar). Volume: cerca de 10 séries por músculo por semana é um mínimo geral, volumes maiores podem ajudar músculos defasados (ciclos de especialização), e as séries semanais não devem subir mais de 20% por ciclo de ~4 semanas. Frequência: sem benefício com volume equalizado, mas limitar o volume por sessão a cerca de 10 séries por músculo e aumentar a frequência para mais volume. Descanso: pelo menos 2 min em multiarticulares e 60–90 s em monoarticulares ou máquinas. Seleção de exercícios: combinar exercícios multi e monoarticulares em diferentes planos e, quando aplicável, priorizar comprimentos musculares longos. Iniciantes não precisam treinar perto da falha, enquanto praticantes altamente treinados podem levar algumas séries à falha, com moderação e principalmente em exercícios monoarticulares ou em máquinas. Técnicas avançadas não mostram vantagem empírica para hipertrofia, mas também nenhum prejuízo aparente, e o aeróbio não parece interferir em volumes moderados (sessões separadas ou musculação antes). Consenso narrativo, sem graduação formal da evidência.

sources.title: Training volume increases or maintenance based on previous volume: the effects on muscular adaptations in trained males
sources.authors: Barsuhn A, Wadhi T, Murphy A, Zazzo S, Thompson B, Barakat C, Bradshaw J, Walters J, Andersen JC, Schoenfeld BJ, Ugrinowitsch C, De Souza EO
sources.summaryEn: RCT in trained men (55 randomized, 29 completed) who maintained their habitual weekly lower-body set volume or increased it by 30% or 60%, training twice weekly for 8 weeks. Muscle thickness and thigh fat-free mass increased in all groups with no group differences (ΣMT +1.07 cm maintain, +0.76 cm at +30%, +0.70 cm at +60%). All groups increased squat 1RM; a main group effect showed higher overall 1RM in the maintenance group (174.7 vs 159.0 and 149.0 kg), which is not a group-by-time interaction, and only the +30% group improved repetitions to failure. High dropout limits precision.
sources.summaryPt: ECR com homens treinados (55 randomizados, 29 concluíram) que mantiveram o volume semanal habitual de séries de membros inferiores ou o aumentaram em 30% ou 60%, treinando duas vezes por semana durante 8 semanas. A espessura muscular e a massa magra da coxa aumentaram em todos os grupos, sem diferença entre eles (soma da espessura +1,07 cm mantendo, +0,76 cm com +30%, +0,70 cm com +60%). Todos os grupos aumentaram o 1RM de agachamento; um efeito principal de grupo mostrou 1RM geral maior no grupo de manutenção (174,7 vs 159,0 e 149,0 kg), o que não é uma interação grupo-tempo, e apenas o grupo +30% melhorou as repetições até a falha. A alta desistência limita a precisão.

sources.title: Effects of Different Volume-Equated Resistance Training Loading Strategies on Muscular Adaptations in Well-Trained Men
sources.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Ratamess NA, Peterson MD, Contreras B, Sonmez GT, Alvar BA
sources.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
sources.summaryEn: In this RCT, 17 well-trained young men were randomized to a bodybuilding-type program (3 sets of 10RM, 90-s rest) or a powerlifting-type program (7 sets of 3RM, 3-min rest), with volume load equated, for 8 weeks. Biceps brachii thickness increased similarly in both groups. Bench press 1RM improved more with the powerlifting-type program, with a trend for squat 1RM. Matching the growth of the 10RM program took more than twice as many heavy sets per exercise. The sample was small and only one muscle was measured.
sources.summaryPt: Neste ECR, 17 homens jovens bem treinados foram randomizados para um programa tipo fisiculturismo (3 séries de 10RM, 90 s de descanso) ou tipo powerlifting (7 séries de 3RM, 3 min de descanso), com volume-carga equalizado, por 8 semanas. A espessura do bíceps braquial aumentou de forma semelhante nos dois grupos. O 1RM no supino melhorou mais com o programa tipo powerlifting, com tendência no agachamento. Igualar o crescimento do programa de 10RM exigiu mais que o dobro de séries pesadas por exercício. A amostra foi pequena e apenas um músculo foi medido.

sources.title: The impact of resistance training on gluteus maximus hypertrophy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.authors: Krause Neto W, Krause TLV, Gama EF
sources.summaryEn: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 studies on gluteus maximus hypertrophy from loaded hip-extension exercise. Resistance training had a moderate effect (11 studies, SMD 0.71, 95% CI 0.50-0.91, I2 = 22%), similar for single-exercise (7 studies, SMD 0.74, I2 = 52%) and combined-exercise (6 studies, SMD 0.68, I2 = 0%) protocols. Hip thrusts, parallel or full back squats, leg press and kneeling hip extensions all increased gluteus maximus size. The literature is small and heterogeneous, and the authors' suggestion to prioritize the hip thrust for isolated glute emphasis is not a head-to-head superiority finding.
sources.summaryPt: Revisão sistemática e metanálise de 12 estudos sobre hipertrofia do glúteo máximo com exercícios de extensão de quadril com carga. O treino de força teve efeito moderado (11 estudos, SMD 0,71, IC95% 0,50-0,91, I2 = 22%), semelhante para protocolos de exercício único (7 estudos, SMD 0,74, I2 = 52%) e combinados (6 estudos, SMD 0,68, I2 = 0%). Hip thrust, agachamento paralelo ou completo, leg press e extensão de quadril ajoelhado aumentaram o tamanho do glúteo máximo. A literatura é pequena e heterogênea, e a sugestão dos autores de priorizar o hip thrust para ênfase isolada no glúteo não é um achado de superioridade em comparação direta.

sources.title: Hamstrings Muscle Architecture and Morphology Following 6 wk of an Eccentrically Biased Romanian Deadlift or Nordic Hamstring Exercise Intervention
sources.authors: Crawford SK, Sandberg C, Vlisides J, Thompson Q, Mosiman SJ, Heiderscheit BC, Hickey JT
sources.summaryEn: RCT in 32 healthy young adults (15 women) randomized to eccentrically biased Romanian deadlift or Nordic hamstring training (n = 16 each), 2x/week for 6 weeks, followed by 2 weeks of detraining. Hamstring anatomical cross-sectional area increased about 10% (0.78 cm2) and biceps femoris long head fascicle length about 9%, with no between-group differences. Biceps femoris long head muscle thickness did not change. Fascicle adaptations reverted after detraining while cross-sectional area stayed elevated. The intervention was very short and outcomes were ultrasound-based.
sources.summaryPt: ECR com 32 adultos jovens saudáveis (15 mulheres) randomizados para levantamento terra romeno com ênfase excêntrica ou exercício nórdico (n = 16 cada), 2x/semana por 6 semanas, seguidas de 2 semanas de destreino. A área de secção transversa anatômica dos isquiotibiais aumentou cerca de 10% (0,78 cm2) e o comprimento de fascículo da cabeça longa do bíceps femoral cerca de 9%, sem diferenças entre os grupos. A espessura muscular da cabeça longa do bíceps femoral não mudou. As adaptações de fascículo regrediram após o destreino, enquanto a área de secção transversa permaneceu elevada. A intervenção foi muito curta e os desfechos foram medidos por ultrassom.

sources.title: Hamstrings Hypertrophy Is Specific to the Training Exercise: Nordic Hamstring versus Lengthened State Eccentric Training
sources.authors: Maeo S, Balshaw TG, Nin DZ, Mc Dermott EJ, Osborne T, Cooper NB, Massey GJ, Kong PW, Pain MTG, Folland JP
sources.summaryEn: Forty-two young men (n=14 per group) did 34 sessions over 12 weeks of either Nordic hamstring training or lengthened-state eccentric training, or served as controls. Training participants were randomly assigned. The lengthened-state exercise was eccentrically focused weight-stack knee flexion in an accentuated hip-flexed position. By MRI it produced more hamstring growth (+18% vs +11%) and biceps femoris long head growth (+19% vs +5%) than Nordics, and more aponeurosis enlargement (+9% vs +3%). Nordics preferentially grew the knee flexors that do not extend the hip.
sources.summaryPt: Quarenta e dois homens jovens (n=14 por grupo) fizeram 34 sessões em 12 semanas de flexão nórdica ou de treino excêntrico em estado alongado, ou ficaram como controle. Os participantes treinados foram randomizados. O exercício em estado alongado foi a flexão do joelho com ênfase excêntrica, em máquina de placas, com o quadril bem flexionado. Pela RM ele produziu mais crescimento dos isquiotibiais (+18% vs +11%) e da cabeça longa do bíceps femoral (+19% vs +5%) do que a nórdica, e maior aumento da aponeurose (+9% vs +3%). A nórdica fez crescer preferencialmente os flexores do joelho que não estendem o quadril.

sources.title: Addition of The Barbell Hip Thrust Elicits Greater Increases in Gluteus Maximus Muscle Thickness in Untrained Young Women
sources.authors: Kassiano W, Kunevaliki G, Costa B, Nunes JP, Castro-E-Souza P, Tricoli I, Ribeiro AS, Cyrino ES
sources.journal: International Journal of Strength and Conditioning
sources.summaryEn: RCT in 33 untrained young women randomized to 45-degree leg press plus stiff-leg deadlift (n = 15) or the same two exercises plus the barbell hip thrust (n = 18), 3 days/week for 10 weeks (30 sessions), with B-mode ultrasound gluteus maximus thickness. Both groups increased gluteus maximus thickness, with greater gains when the hip thrust was added (+9.3% vs +6.0%, p = 0.016). The abstract does not indicate that total sets were equated, so the added hip-thrust sets may explain part of the difference. This is a single short trial in untrained women with ultrasound at limited sites.
sources.summaryPt: ECR com 33 mulheres jovens não treinadas randomizadas para leg press 45 graus mais stiff (n = 15) ou os mesmos dois exercícios mais o hip thrust com barra (n = 18), 3 dias/semana por 10 semanas (30 sessões), com espessura do glúteo máximo por ultrassom modo B. Os dois grupos aumentaram a espessura do glúteo máximo, com ganhos maiores quando o hip thrust foi acrescentado (+9,3% vs +6,0%, p = 0,016). O resumo não indica que o total de séries tenha sido equalizado, então as séries extras de hip thrust podem explicar parte da diferença. É um único ensaio curto, com mulheres não treinadas e ultrassom em poucos pontos.

sources.title: Test–Retest Reliability of the One-Repetition Maximum (1RM) Strength Assessment: a Systematic Review
sources.authors: Grgic J, Lazinica B, Schoenfeld BJ, Pedisic Z
sources.summaryEn: This PRISMA systematic review covered 32 studies (pooled n=1595) on the test-retest reliability of 1RM testing. ICCs ranged from 0.64 to 0.99 (median 0.97; 92% were 0.90 or higher), and CVs from 0.5% to 12.1% (median 4.2%). Reliability was generally high regardless of training experience, number of familiarization sessions, single- or multi-joint exercise, body region, sex or age. Most studies found no systematic change between trials. There was no quantitative pooling.
sources.summaryPt: Esta revisão sistemática (PRISMA) reuniu 32 estudos (n total=1595) sobre a confiabilidade teste-reteste do 1RM. Os ICCs variaram de 0,64 a 0,99 (mediana 0,97; 92% iguais ou acima de 0,90) e os CVs de 0,5% a 12,1% (mediana 4,2%). A confiabilidade foi em geral alta, independentemente de experiência de treino, número de sessões de familiarização, exercício uni ou multiarticular, região do corpo, sexo ou idade. A maioria dos estudos não encontrou mudança sistemática entre as tentativas. Não houve agregação quantitativa.

missingTopics.why: Program pages need to justify how sets/reps/load are varied week-to-week and across a mesocycle. Current coverage only touches periodization tangentially via a 2004 narrative review (Kraemer & Ratamess, level D) and the 2009 ACSM position stand. There is no dedicated systematic review/meta-analysis comparing periodization models, despite this being one of the most heavily meta-analyzed topics in strength science.
missingTopics.searchHints: Grgic, Mikulic, Podnar, Pedisic (2017) 'Effects of linear and daily undulating periodized resistance training programs on measures of muscle hypertrophy: a systematic review and meta-analysis', PeerJ, DOI 10.7717/peerj.3695 (verified via Crossref). Companion strength paper: Grgic, Mikulic, Schoenfeld, Bishop, Pedisic (2015?) or similar, 'Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Linear and Undulating Periodized Resistance Training Programs on Muscular Strength', Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, DOI 10.1519/jsc.0000000000000712 (verified). Also consider Rhea, Ball, Phillips, Burkett (2002) JSCR original linear-vs-undulating RCT for historical context.

missingTopics.why: 1RM estimation is a core feature (percent-based programming, calculators) but current support is only C/D level and decades old (Brzycki 1993 single-study, LeSuer 1997). A modern systematic review/meta-analysis on prediction-equation accuracy, including load-velocity-based estimation, is missing and would raise this topic to A/B level.
missingTopics.searchHints: LeMense, Malone, Kinderman, Fedewa, Winchester (2024) 'Validity of Using the Load-Velocity Relationship to Estimate 1 Repetition Maximum in the Back Squat Exercise: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis', Journal of Strength & Conditioning Research, DOI 10.1519/jsc.0000000000004709 (verified via Crossref). Also: Fitas, Pezarat-Correia, Mendonca (2025) 'Reliability of the two-point method... and its validity in estimating the one-repetition maximum using the load–velocity relationship of the free-weight back squat', Applied Physiology, Nutrition, and Metabolism, DOI 10.1139/apnm-2024-0546 (verified).

missingTopics.topic: Menstrual cycle phase effects on training performance/adaptation (women-specific)
missingTopics.why: The task explicitly requires 'women' as a covered topic, but the only entry (Roberts 2020) addresses aggregate sex differences in adaptation, not the practical question of whether/how to adjust training across the menstrual cycle — a frequently asked, evidence-relevant question for a science-first app targeting female users.
missingTopics.searchHints: McNulty, Elliott-Sale, Dolan, Swinton, Ansdell, Goodall, Thomas, Hicks (2020) 'The Effects of Menstrual Cycle Phase on Exercise Performance in Eumenorrheic Women: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis', Sports Medicine, DOI 10.1007/s40279-020-01319-3 (verified via Crossref, plus a companion 2020 Sports Medicine paper by the same group on oral contraceptives and exercise performance).

missingTopics.topic: Resistance-training-specific warm-up protocol (not general sport warm-up)
missingTopics.why: Warm-up is currently backed only by Fradkin et al. 2010, a general sports-performance warm-up meta-analysis (level A but not resistance-training-specific — no guidance on ramping sets, specific-vs-general warm-up, or number of warm-up sets before working sets on a lift like bench/squat).
missingTopics.searchHints: McCrary, Ackermann, Halaki (2015) 'A systematic review of the effects of upper body warm-up on performance and injury', British Journal of Sports Medicine, DOI 10.1136/bjsports-2014-094228 (verified via Crossref — directly addresses bench-press-style warm-up protocols).

missingTopics.why: Explicitly named in the required exercise catalog ('shrugs') but has zero citations of any level in current coverage. A targeted Crossref search found no dedicated hypertrophy/strength RCT for the shrug — closest available literature is EMG/biomechanics work on the shrug phase of the power clean, which is a genuine literature gap a sports scientist should flag rather than force-fit.
missingTopics.searchHints: Comfort, Allen, Graham-Smith (2011) 'Kinetic Comparisons During Variations of the Power Clean' JSCR, or Comfort et al. 'Characteristics of the Shrug Motion and Trapezius Muscle Activity During the Power Clean', Journal of Strength & Conditioning Research, DOI 10.1519/jsc.0000000000003355 (verified real, 2021, but Olympic-lift context, not isolated shrug hypertrophy — flag as best-available-evidence caveat).

missingTopics.topic: Face pull / rear-delt & external rotation for shoulder health
missingTopics.why: Explicitly named in the exercise catalog ('face pull') and current rear_delt coverage is only C-level (Schoenfeld 2013, hand position on reverse fly EMG). No study addresses the face pull specifically or its common rationale (posterior shoulder balance / shoulder health for pressing athletes).
missingTopics.searchHints: Look for EMG comparisons of face pull vs. reverse fly vs. band pull-apart on posterior deltoid/infraspinatus/lower trapezius (search terms: 'face pull electromyography posterior deltoid infraspinatus'); also consider Reinold, Macrina, Wilk et al. (2004, Am J Sports Med) rotator cuff/scapular stabilizer EMG work as the closest validated evidence for the rationale, since no face-pull-specific RCT was found via Crossref.

missingTopics.topic: Forearm/grip training for hypertrophy and strength
missingTopics.why: Explicitly named in the exercise catalog ('forearms') with essentially no coverage — only a tangential brachioradialis EMG mention inside a biceps-curl-variant paper (Marcolin 2018, C level). Repeated Crossref searches for dedicated forearm/wrist-flexor hypertrophy training studies returned no relevant sports-science RCTs, indicating this is a real literature-thin area.
missingTopics.searchHints: Search 'wrist flexor extensor training muscle hypertrophy' and 'grip strength training program forearm size' in Crossref/PubMed; also check strongman/climbing-science literature (e.g., journals like Journal of Strength & Conditioning Research, International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance) for grip/forearm-specific protocols — if none found, note in the app that forearm guidance rests on extrapolation from general hypertrophy principles rather than exercise-specific RCTs.

missingTopics.why: Explicitly named in the exercise catalog ('adductors/abductors'). Existing coverage (Ishøi 2016 Copenhagen Adduction) is injury-prevention framed for a bodyweight eccentric exercise, not machine-based hypertrophy training, and Moore 2020 covers glute medius/minimus generally but not adductor machines. Crossref searches for adductor/abductor machine hypertrophy studies returned only rehab/gait/EMG papers unrelated to gym training.
missingTopics.searchHints: Search 'hip adductor machine EMG bodybuilders' and 'seated hip abduction adduction resistance training muscle activation'; check Distefano et al. (2009, J Orthop Sports Phys Ther) gluteal EMG methodology as an analog approach; note to the team this exercise pair may need to be justified via general principles (mechanical tension, EMG-based exercise selection) rather than a dedicated hypertrophy RCT, since none was located.

missingTopics.topic: Leg extension knee safety (open- vs closed-kinetic-chain loading)
missingTopics.why: Leg extension is a named catalog exercise and a common 'is it bad for your knees' question for a safety-conscious app, but current leg_extension coverage (Pedrosa 2022) addresses ROM/hypertrophy only, not joint-loading safety in healthy trainees (existing hits on this topic are ACL-reconstruction rehab papers, a different population).
missingTopics.searchHints: Search for general-population (non-rehab) patellofemoral/tibiofemoral loading comparisons between leg press, squat, and leg extension, e.g. work by Escamilla or Wilk on knee joint forces during open- vs closed-kinetic-chain exercise in healthy lifters, distinct from the ACL-reconstruction-specific IJSPT 2021 paper found (DOI 10.26603/001c.18983), which is post-surgical and not directly generalizable.

No study addresses barbell vs. dumbbell vs. machine overhead press for hypertrophy/strength outcomes, or shoulder-loading considerations specific to overhead pressing, despite this being a primary shoulder exercise in the catalog.
missingTopics.searchHints: Search 'overhead press barbell dumbbell machine hypertrophy strength comparison' and 'landmine press vs overhead press shoulder EMG'; also check Saeterbakken's other work (e.g., 2016-2019 papers on shoulder press stability/EMG) beyond the 2013 seated-vs-standing paper already cited.
